parts.visual:
You realize an employee is failing. You think: 'Maybe if I train them more, they will improve.' Six months later, they haven't improved, the company lost money, and you fire them anyway. You wasted six months.

The Axiom:
1. Hire Slow: Take extreme caution before bringing someone into the company. Do 5 interviews. Check every reference. Test their actual skills.
2. Fire Fast: The moment you realize you made a mistake, terminate the employment immediately. Do not hope for a miracle.
parts.audio: 'Hire Slow, Fire Fast' is the most famous management mantra in Silicon Valley. Most amateur founders do the exact opposite: they hire fast out of panic, and they fire slow out of guilt.

questions.question: A new marketing director has been at the startup for 30 days. They are consistently missing deadlines and making excuses. The CEO has a 'gut feeling' this person is a disaster. What should the CEO do?
options: Give them 6 more months to figure it out.
Fire them immediately. If someone is a disaster in their first 30 days (when they should be on their best behavior), they will only get worse. Rip the band-aid off now.
questions.correct_answer: Fire them immediately. If someone is a disaster in their first 30 days (when they should be on their best behavior), they will only get worse. Rip the band-aid off now.
questions.explanation: Trust your gut. Prolonging the inevitable only hurts the company.

questions.question: Listen to the founder explaining how they interview candidates. Why is 'Hiring Slow' effective?
questions.tts_text: We don't just ask them questions. We pay them to work with us on a real project for one weekend. You can lie in an interview, but you cannot fake the ability to execute under pressure.
options: It filters out the 'Professional Interviewers'. By forcing candidates to do actual work, the startup protects itself from hiring charismatic people who are actually incompetent at the job.
questions.correct_answer: It filters out the 'Professional Interviewers'. By forcing candidates to do actual work, the startup protects itself from hiring charismatic people who are actually incompetent at the job.
questions.explanation: Past execution is the only predictor of future execution.

questions.question: Why is 'Firing Slow' considered a betrayal of your best employees (the A-Players)?
options: Because the A-Players are forced to do the failing employee's work to keep the company alive. If the CEO tolerates incompetence, the A-Players will lose respect for the CEO and quit.
Because they want to be fired.
questions.correct_answer: Because the A-Players are forced to do the failing employee's work to keep the company alive. If the CEO tolerates incompetence, the A-Players will lose respect for the CEO and quit.
questions.explanation: Tolerating mediocrity is an insult to excellence.

questions.question: What is the psychological barrier that stops founders from 'Firing Fast'?
options: They forget how to do it.
Empathy and Conflict Avoidance. Firing someone is emotionally brutal. Founders feel guilty for ruining someone's livelihood, so they invent excuses to delay the painful conversation.
questions.correct_answer: Empathy and Conflict Avoidance. Firing someone is emotionally brutal. Founders feel guilty for ruining someone's livelihood, so they invent excuses to delay the painful conversation.
questions.explanation: A CEO's empathy must be for the survival of the company, not the comfort of one failing employee.

pairs.match: Taking a rigorous, cautious approach to selecting candidates
Terminating an employee immediately once it is clear they are a bad fit
The psychological tendency to delay difficult conversations or actions
Paying a candidate to do real work before offering them a full-time job
